Work in /opt/nxeon. Build the CARD AUTO-CHARGE billing engine for subscription renewals. Read `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` and `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` for context (do not edit them).

TODAY: renewals debit the wallet only (`worker/billing.ts` `debitWallet`); on `InsufficientBalanceError` the server enters grace and is then SUSPENDED. `User.stripePaymentMethodId` is never written or read. A customer with a perfectly good card gets suspended when their wallet empties. `grep sendMail worker/*.ts` returns NOTHING — a suspension produces only a bell icon in a portal the customer has stopped visiting.

YOU OWN EXACTLY: `worker/billing.ts`, `lib/stripe-cards.ts` (create), `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` (create), `components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx`, new files under `components/customer/billing/`, `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`, `components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx`, `lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts`. NOTHING else — several agents run concurrently. `prisma/schema.prisma` is FROZEN.

SCHEMA ALREADY EXISTS FOR YOU: `User.cardBrand/cardLast4/cardExpMonth/cardExpYear/cardExpiryNotifiedAt`; `Server.dunningStage` (Int, 0 = current, 1..N failed card attempts) / `dunningNextAt` / `dunningPayUrl`; `WalletTransaction.stripePaymentIntentId` (@unique — your idempotency guard for crediting an off-session charge); `Server.suspendReason` ("UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN" — only UNPAID may be auto-lifted or terminated).

DESIGN AGREED WITH THE OWNER — implement exactly this:
- **Wallet credit applied FIRST, card auto-charged for the remainder.** Matches `lib/wallet-split.ts` which checkout already uses, so renewals behave like purchases, and prepaid/referral/refund credit gets drained instead of accumulating as a liability.
- **Dunning retries on days 1, 3 and 5**, each with an email. Suspend ONLY after retries are exhausted. `DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` is already exported from `lib/mailer.ts` — import it; hardcoding will make the email copy lie about attempts remaining.

IMPLEMENT:
1. **Save a card** — Stripe Checkout in `mode: "setup"` (no Stripe Elements exists in this codebase). Store the payment method on the Stripe customer, on `User.stripePaymentMethodId`, and mirror the display fields. Import `stripe()`/`stripeConfigured()` from `lib/stripe.ts` — do NOT edit that file. If you need an API route under `app/api/stripe/**` (owned elsewhere), put your entry point in your own server action and report the route you'd want.
2. **Off-session charge** — apply wallet credit first via `walletSplit`, then charge the remainder `confirm: true, off_session: true` with a Stripe **idempotency key derived from serverId + billing period**. On success credit the wallet by the charged amount (guarded by `stripePaymentIntentId` UNIQUE, catching P2002) and let the EXISTING CAS-guarded transaction debit the full `renewCents` — mirroring how checkout works (card credits wallet, wallet pays the bill) so a partial failure cannot half-apply. Respect Stripe's ~$0.50 minimum; `walletSplit` already solves that.
3. **Failure handling** — distinguish `requires_action` (3-D Secure), hard decline, and transient error. For 3DS and self-service payment, generate a hosted Checkout link for the outstanding amount, store on `Server.dunningPayUrl`, and email it (reuses the proven checkout+credit path instead of client-side Stripe.js). Advance `dunningStage`, set `dunningNextAt` on the 1/3/5 schedule, suspend only when exhausted (and set `suspendReason: "UNPAID"`). Reset `dunningStage` to 0 on any successful renewal.
4. **Send the emails** — six templates already exist on `emails.*` in `lib/mailer.ts` with ZERO senders: `paymentReceipt`, `paymentFailed` (use the 5-positional-string overload, NOT the object form — an older object-form overload exists for the admin previewer), `paymentRetryFailed`, `paymentActionRequired`, `paymentFinalNotice`, `cardExpiringSoon`. Wire them all.
5. **Make the admin dunning panel real** — `components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx` exposes `dunning_grace_days` / `dunning_warn_days` / `dunning_terminate_days` that NOTHING reads; the worker uses env vars instead. Make the worker read the admin settings with env as fallback.
6. **Billing UI** — card-on-file section ("Visa ···· 4242, expires 04/28"), add/replace/remove. `components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx` exists but is deliberately NOT MOUNTED (import commented out in `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`, replaced by a "Coming soon" card, with the reason documented — that was the right call while unwired). Now that off-session charging exists, either wire it properly or delete the dead component and the fake card. Do not leave a third dead control.

REQUIREMENTS
- Real money. A retried sweep must never double-charge; a captured payment must never be lost. Every once-only write needs a UNIQUE constraint and a P2002 catch.
- Match the Nxeon dark theme; reuse `.card`, `.btn-primary`, `Badge`, existing slate/brand/navy classes. No new visual styles.
- Copy must be plain and non-blaming — a declined card is usually the bank's doing. Never state the service is suspended when it isn't.
- Comment style: explain WHY, cite the real failure prevented.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`/`npm run dev`, do NOT restart any systemd service (production is live).
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`.
- Do NOT git commit/push, do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, do NOT write to the live database, do NOT make live Stripe charges.

Report: the charging flow end to end, your idempotency keys, the dunning schedule as built, which emails fire when, and what you did about AutoRecharge.

**File:** `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:652-675`

Uses `requireUser()` → `currentUser()`, which returns the **impersonated** user, and is strictly
owner-only (no admin bypass at `:662`) — so impersonation is the only way an admin reaches it. It
returns the mailbox plaintext and creates **no `auditLog` entry at all** (contrast
`resetMailboxPassword` at `:717`).

*Failure:* admin impersonates customer B → `revealMailboxPassword` → plaintext IMAP/SMTP password →
exit impersonation → log into B's email directly. Zero trace.

## P1-5. The "Auto-suspend overdue accounts" toggle and all three dunning-day fields are dead

**Files:** `components/admin/settings/BillingPanel.tsx:22-26, :43-48`; `lib/actions-settings.ts:51`;
`worker/billing.ts:27, 31, 33`

`auto_suspend_enabled`, `dunning_grace_days`, `dunning_warn_days` and `dunning_terminate_days` are
written to the `Setting` table and have **zero reads anywhere in the repo** (verified by whole-repo
grep, excluding the settings plumbing itself). The sweep at `worker/billing.ts:192-215` suspends
unconditionally and reads `process.env.NXEON_GRACE_DAYS ?? 3` / `NXEON_TERMINATE_DAYS ?? 10` /
`NXEON_WARN_BEFORE_TERMINATE_DAYS ?? 2` — **none of which are set in `.env`**, so the values are
hardcoded 3/10/2 regardless of what the panel shows.

*Failure:* an incident forces the operator to pause suspensions. They turn the toggle **off**, see
"Saved.", and within 10 minutes the sweep queues `SUSPEND` jobs and knocks customer VMs offline anyway.

## P1-6. The Settings → Email template editor is completely inert

**Files:** `components/admin/settings/EmailPanel.tsx:19`, `lib/actions-email-templates.ts`,
`lib/email-render.ts:220-249`, `lib/mailer.ts:118-128, 166-175`

The editor saves to `db.emailTemplate` (20 seeded rows, all `enabled: true` — confirmed in the live
DB). The only code path that reads those rows is `renderTemplate()`, reachable only via
`sendMail({ template })` / `sendTemplate()` — and **those have zero call sites.** Every real send
passes explicit `subject` + `html` from the hardcoded catalog: `lib/actions.ts:135-136` (welcome),
`lib/actions-account.ts:129-130, 171-172` (password reset), `lib/stripe.ts:254-255` (receipt),
`lib/actions-newsletter-campaign.ts:204`.

*Failure:* admin rewrites the "Welcome" subject and body, sees **"Saved."**
(`EmailTemplateEditor.tsx:160`), and every new customer still receives the untouched hardcoded
template. The enable/disable checkbox (`:237`) is equally inert.

## Suggested order of work

**Launch blockers — do not take paying customers until these are done.**

1. **P0-1** (email takeover) and **P0-2** (2FA oracle) — security, exploitable today, hours of work
   each. P0-1 is two schema constraints plus a `verified` gate — **P1-29 falls out with it**, since
   both are the same missing gate.
2. **P0-4**, **P0-5** and **P0-9** — three small guard/flag changes, each preventing irreversible
   customer data loss. Cheapest risk reduction in the whole list.
3. **P0-3** (Stripe fulfilment) — the largest refactor here, but the highest-frequency money failure.
4. **P0-8** (`suspendReason`) and **P1-1** (worker deadlock) — a single enum field and a single
   `reject()` respectively.
5. **P0-6** (proration) and **P0-7** (refunds) — fix before any volume of upgrade or refund traffic
   exists, because both are far harder to unwind retroactively than to prevent.

**Before the first support ticket.**

6. **P1-5** (dunning controls) — an operator needs a working suspension kill switch on day one.
7. **P1-2** (admin gate does not cover `/api/admin/*`) and **P1-3** (impersonation spend guard).
8. **P1-37** and **P1-19**/**P1-40** — refusals that vanish, and a build state that locks an account
   out permanently with no customer-reachable escape. These generate tickets nobody can resolve.

**Then the honesty sweep.** For each of the ~25 write-only preferences and settings (P1-6 through
P1-12, P1-24, P1-27, P1-31 through P1-36, P1-41): **wire it or remove it.** A control that reports
success and does nothing is worse than an absent one — it converts a missing feature into a broken
promise, and in the case of WHOIS privacy, notification consent and SSL expiry, into a compliance or
security claim the platform cannot honour. `AutoRecharge` is the template.

**Finally**, the features that cannot work at all (P1-14 downgrades, P1-7 coupons, P1-25 bandwidth
metering, P1-22 apps, P1-23 game settings) — each needs a product decision first: finish it, or pull it
from the UI before launch. Pulling is a one-line change and is the right answer for most of them.
